subject: Workplace Skills
title: Giving Credit Generously
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Giving Credit Generously.

hook.text: A director always said 'The team did this.' His team would walk through walls for him.

buildup.text: Credit hoarding is the fastest way to lose allies. People stop contributing when their work is stolen.

discovery.text: Giving credit publicly makes people want to work with you again. Your reputation as a collaborator grows.

twist.text: Giving credit doesn't diminish you. Research shows people who share credit are rated as more competent.

climax.text: Name specific contributions: 'Rosa's analysis surfaced the pattern that changed our approach.'

punchline.text: Share credit loudly. It comes back with interest.

quiz.question: What happens when leaders share credit with their teams?
options: They appear less competent to senior leadership
They are rated as more competent and earn stronger loyalty
Team members become complacent and stop working hard
